snapshot.title: Orchard Standpipe Security Breach — Precautionary Boil-Water Advisory

fields.org: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer
fields.headline: City Confirms Malicious Act at Orchard Standpipe; Precautionary Boil-Water Advisory Issued for Hilltop Zone
fields.subhead: Water quality integrity compromised; use bottled water until further notice.
fields.body:
The City of Millbrook has confirmed a malevolent act at the Orchard Standpipe facility. A physical intrusion occurred overnight, resulting in the compromise of water quality at the outlet point. The City’s Water Quality Manager has verified a sustained drop in chlorine residual to 0.7 mg/L, and lab analysis confirms no instrument error or system fault.

A precautionary boil-water advisory is now in effect for Zone 2, covering the Hilltop area. No drinking water is safe until further notice. The City urges all residents in Zone 2 to use bottled water for consumption, cooking, and brushing teeth.

The site has been secured by Millbrook Police and the FBI is conducting a joint investigation. The City is working with the Ohio EPA Division of Drinking Water and the Carver County Health Commissioner to ensure public safety. The Joint Information Center has been activated, and updates will be issued via MillbrookAlert, the city website, and official social media accounts.

This is not a routine event. The City will not discuss ransom demands or attack details. All information released will follow the Public Communications Plan (MDWS-PCP-2026), Section 5.4.
fields.boilerplate: The City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer provides safe, reliable drinking water to over 120,000 residents across 14 zones. The Department operates under the Emergency Response Plan (MDWS-ERP-2026), the Public Communications Plan (MDWS-PCP-2026), and the OT/Cybersecurity Plan (MDWS-OTSEC-2026). All operations are monitored 24/7 from the Central Control Room, located at 1000 Millbrook Way, Millbrook, OH 43050.

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject confirms the public narrative shift to a formal advisory. The PIO must validate that the language matches the approved template in MDWS-PCP-2026, Section 5.4, and that the statement on a malevolent act and water quality compromise is intact. Watch for delays in escalation to the Director or WQ.
